note: Independently re-judged from the complete RFC 4271 Section 8.2.2 OpenSent action list and RFC 6608 Section 4. TestRFC4271OpenSentUnexpectedMessageIsAnFSMError retains four distinct real TCP inputs: Cease NOTIFICATION (Event 25), KEEPALIVE (26), empty UPDATE (27), and malformed withdrawn-length UPDATE (28). Each requires exactly one 5/1 response, TCP closure rather than a read timeout, stopped ConnectRetry/Hold/Keepalive timers, released session and ConnectRetryCounter 0 to 1. The older readUntil helper accepts a non-timeout read error as closure; this note does not call that a strict io.EOF assertion. The shared FSM catchall producer contains the same retry-counter/state transition for the listed timer/connection events; the peer matrix directly exercises received-message events. TestRFC4271ExpectedMessagesRaiseNoFSMError distinguishes a valid OPEN and subsequent legitimate KEEPALIVE/UPDATE with a live retained session and counter zero. The separate Event 24 control sends 2/1, requires no NOTIFICATION, closure/release and unchanged nonzero counter 3. These boundary controls distinguish state and version-error classification rather than merely another malformed packet. The renewed native records retain clean-green and named-unit-red observations, including the version-error claim renewal. The updated-by marker correctly adds the RFC 6608 subcode/Data obligation without removing the base teardown list. These base tests do not assert the one-octet Data; the updater is audited separately.
